key_insight: A CNF-interlayered spray-coated bioplastic multilayer can substantially improve the oxygen and moisture barrier performance of Broussonetia papyrifera fiber paper while preserving a sustainable paper-based substrate.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable packaging-surface engineering route for converting low-cost cellulose paper into higher-performance biodegradable barrier materials.
method: Spray-coat a paper substrate derived from Broussonetia papyrifera fibers
Add a cellulose nanofibril (CNF) interlayer to block coating penetration and smooth the surface
Apply outer biodegradable bioplastic coatings: PPC, PHAs, and PPC/PHA blends
evidence_signal: Compared with uncoated paper, the coated multilayer systems showed improved mechanical properties and better oxygen and water vapor barrier performance, with blend formulations giving balanced barrier behavior.
watch_item: Practical deployment still depends on replacing conventional organic-solvent processing with greener, non-toxic solvent systems.
paper_title: Enhancing the barrier performance of paper derived from Broussonetia papyrifera L. fibers through a spray coating process
